description: How game characters sense, move, decide, plan and learn within a strict frame budget. Students implement steering, A* pathfinding, behaviour trees, utility and planning systems, influence maps and tree search for classic games such as Oware, then test the results with bots.
modelledOn: Buckland, Programming Game AI by Example
Browne et al., A Survey of Monte Carlo Tree Search Methods
outcomes: Implement kinematic and steering behaviours and combine them into believable group movement.
Implement and compare A*, hierarchical and navigation-mesh pathfinding on game maps and justify heuristic choices.
Design character decision making with finite state machines, behaviour trees, utility systems and goal-oriented planning.
Build tactical analysis tools such as influence maps and cover selection for squad behaviour.
Implement minimax, alpha-beta and Monte Carlo tree search for turn-based games.
Evaluate game AI with automated playtesting, profiling and simple learning agents.

units.title: Foundations of game AI
topics: Game AI versus academic AI: believability, fun and fairness over optimality; the sense-think-act loop
AI architecture inside a game loop: frame budgets, time slicing, scheduling and level of detail
Difficulty and fairness: randomness, rubber-banding and dynamic difficulty adjustment
World knowledge and perception: blackboards, sight and hearing models, memory of the player

units.title: Steering and movement
topics: Kinematic movement: seek, flee, arrive and wander
Steering behaviours: velocity matching, align, face, pursue and evade
Delegated steering: path following, separation and obstacle avoidance
Flocking with boids and crowd simulation
Combining behaviours: weighted blending, priority arbitration and steering pipelines
Predicting motion: projectile aiming and jump planning

units.title: Pathfinding
topics: Graph representations of game worlds: tile grids, waypoint graphs and navigation meshes
Dijkstra's algorithm and A*: open and closed lists, admissible and consistent heuristics
Heuristic design and tie-breaking; weighted A*, IDA* and memory limits
Hierarchical pathfinding and jump point search for large maps
Navigation meshes: generation and the funnel algorithm for smooth paths
Dynamic worlds: D* Lite, replanning and local avoidance with reciprocal velocity obstacles

units.title: Decision making
topics: Decision trees and their authoring limits
Finite state machines: hierarchical and pushdown variants, transitions and state explosion
Behaviour trees: sequence, selector, decorator and parallel nodes with a blackboard
Rule-based systems and fuzzy logic for graded decisions
Utility-based AI: response curves, scoring and action selection

units.title: Goal-oriented behaviour and planning
topics: Goal-oriented behaviour: goals, insistence and discontent
Goal-oriented action planning: STRIPS-style actions with preconditions and effects, searched with A*
Hierarchical task networks and task decomposition
Plan execution: monitoring, invalidation and replanning
Comparing FSM, behaviour tree, utility and planner designs for authoring cost and emergent behaviour

units.title: Tactical and strategic AI
topics: Waypoint tactics and cover point selection
Influence maps: propagation, decay and terrain analysis
Tactical pathfinding with danger costs
Coordinated action: squads, formations and strategy layers in real-time strategy games
The AI director: pacing and encounter generation in survival and shooter games

units.title: Adversarial search and Monte Carlo tree search
topics: Minimax and alpha-beta pruning with move ordering
Evaluation functions, iterative deepening and transposition tables
Expectimax for games with dice, such as Ludo and backgammon
Monte Carlo tree search and UCT: selection, expansion, simulation and backpropagation
Case study: AI for Oware (Ayo) and Ludo, comparing search depth with simulation count

units.title: Learning agents and AI testing
topics: Reinforcement learning in games: Q-learning on a grid world and function approximation
Imitation learning from player traces and behaviour cloning
Neuroevolution and genetic algorithms for tuning agents
Automated playtesting: bots, coverage of game states and balance metrics
Debugging, visualising and profiling AI; determinism and replay for reproducible bugs
Player modelling and the ethics of adaptive difficulty and engagement design

schedule.title: What game AI is
schedule.exercise: Pick a game you know and write a half-page analysis of its AI: what the characters sense, what they decide, and where the designers cheat to keep it fun.

tasks.title: Review a case of a stealth game enemy that feels unfair, decide which sensing and reaction rules to change and score your choices against the rubric
Step an AI scheduler through ten agents with a 2 millisecond frame budget and record which agents get time-sliced and delayed
Implement dynamic difficulty adjustment for an endless runner using a rolling success rate and show how the spawn rate responds over 200 rounds

schedule.title: Kinematic movement and basic steering
schedule.exercise: Derive the arrive behaviour with a slowing radius and explain in writing how the radii and time-to-target change the final approach.

tasks.title: Implement seek, flee and arrive for a point agent and plot its trajectory to a moving target for three slowing radii
Implement pursue and evade by predicting the target position and compare the capture time against plain seek over 50 random starts
Build path following with separation and obstacle avoidance for five agents crossing a marketplace map and report the number of collisions

schedule.title: Groups, blending and prediction
schedule.exercise: Describe how you would tune boid weights to get a convincing crowd leaving a stadium, and list two failure modes of weighted blending.

tasks.title: Implement boids with separation, alignment and cohesion for 50 agents and measure how flock spread changes as each weight varies
Combine seek, avoidance and separation with a priority arbiter, compare it with weighted blending and report where each gets stuck
Compute the launch angle and speed that hit a moving target under gravity, and test the aimer on 30 random target paths

schedule.title: Grids, graphs and A*
schedule.exercise: Prove that Manhattan distance is admissible on a 4-connected grid and show by example when it stops being admissible with diagonal moves.

tasks.title: Step Dijkstra and then A* on a 10 by 10 grid, recording open and closed lists and comparing the number of nodes expanded
Compare Manhattan, Euclidean and octile heuristics on three maps with walls and report nodes expanded and path cost for each
Implement weighted A* and plot path cost against nodes expanded for weights from 1 to 5 on a 64 by 64 map

schedule.title: Large maps and navigation meshes
schedule.exercise: Choose a pathfinding stack for a large open-world city map with moving vehicles, and justify each layer against the memory and time budget.

tasks.title: Build a two-level abstraction of a 40 by 40 map and compare hierarchical search with flat A* on path length and nodes expanded
Apply the funnel algorithm to a corridor of triangles to turn a jagged centre-line path into a smooth shortest path
Implement replanning when a door closes mid-route using D* Lite and compare its work with rerunning A* from scratch

schedule.title: Decision making architectures
schedule.exercise: Model a guard character in three ways, as a finite state machine, a behaviour tree and a utility system, and compare how each handles a new behaviour.

tasks.title: Draw and step a hierarchical state machine for a patrol-chase-search guard and list the transitions that cause flip-flopping
Implement a behaviour tree with selector, sequence and decorator nodes for a shopkeeper character and log which nodes succeed each tick
Build a utility system for a farm-sim worker with response curves for hunger, distance and urgency and tune it to avoid oscillation

schedule.title: Goals and planning
schedule.exercise: Write STRIPS-style actions for a character who must cook a meal, with preconditions and effects, and hand-trace the plan found.

tasks.title: Implement goal-oriented behaviour with insistence values for a villager and report the discontent score of each choice as the day proceeds
Search a small action set with A* over world states to find a plan that reaches a goal, and view the plan graph
Decompose a compound task into primitive tasks with a hierarchical task network and compare plan length and search effort against flat planning

schedule.title: Execution, replanning and design trade-offs
schedule.exercise: Compare FSM, behaviour tree, utility and planner approaches for a game of your choice in a decision table covering authoring cost, debugging and emergent behaviour.

tasks.title: Execute a plan step by step while an event invalidates a precondition, and show when the agent should replan rather than continue
Add plan monitoring to a planner so it detects an invalidated step, replans and logs the number of replans over 100 randomised runs
Choose an AI architecture for a given game brief in a case, justify the trade-offs and score your choice against the rubric

schedule.title: Tactical and strategic AI
schedule.exercise: Sketch the influence maps that a strategy-game AI would keep to decide where to expand, defend and attack, and say how often each should update.

tasks.title: Score candidate cover points by exposure to a threat and distance to the agent, then pick and justify the best point
Compute an influence map from unit positions with propagation and decay on a 30 by 30 grid and mark the frontier between two teams
Run tactical pathfinding where cell cost includes danger from the influence map and compare the route with the shortest path

schedule.title: Minimax and alpha-beta
schedule.exercise: Show by hand how alpha-beta prunes a given game tree for good and bad move ordering and state the best-case complexity.

tasks.title: Step minimax and then alpha-beta on a game tree of depth 4 and count nodes saved by pruning for two move orderings
Write an evaluation function for Oware using seeds in store, mobility and captures, and pit depth-4 search against a random mover
Evaluate a Ludo-style position with expectimax over dice outcomes and compare the chosen move with the minimax choice

schedule.title: Monte Carlo tree search
schedule.exercise: Explain how the UCT exploration constant changes search behaviour and design an experiment to choose it for a game of Oware.

tasks.title: Run four iterations of MCTS by hand on a small tic-tac-toe position, recording selection, expansion, simulation and backpropagation counts
Implement UCT for a connect-style game and plot win rate against the number of simulations from 100 to 5,000
Compare alpha-beta and MCTS agents at equal time budgets in Oware over 100 games and report win rates with confidence intervals

schedule.title: Learning agents
schedule.exercise: Compare reinforcement learning, imitation learning and evolution as ways to produce a racing-game opponent, listing the data and compute each needs.

tasks.title: Train a tabular Q-learning agent on a 6 by 6 grid world with traps and plot episode return across 2,000 episodes
Clone behaviour from 500 recorded player moves in a platform game with a decision tree and measure agreement with the player on held-out moves
Evolve the weights of a small controller for a lander game with a genetic algorithm and report fitness per generation

schedule.title: Testing, profiling and ethics
schedule.exercise: Prepare a playtesting and AI quality plan for a mobile game: bots to run, metrics to track, performance limits and a policy on adaptive difficulty.

tasks.title: Run 1,000 bot games of a card game with random and greedy bots and flag any strategy that wins more than 60 percent
Profile an AI update loop, find the slowest agents in the frame timeline and propose time slicing to hold a 4 millisecond budget
Decide in a case whether a game should adapt difficulty or spending prompts to a player's behaviour, and score your reasoning against the rubric
